code_path_observation: Adapter encodes a Python event to JSON bytes, then Writer.write_event reparses those bytes and recursively checks array references before buffering.
Writer reserves candidate block and index capacity for each event. CandidateBudget reduces repeated Path construction but retains per-event reservation work.
Lossless block compression and storage were functioning in S07; 270 blocks and 8,864,998 committed events were verified, far below 4 GiB.
causal_limit: These archived profiles identify likely cost centers but do not measure their causal contribution in the real S07 process. The real B arm had an unfinished U1 guard loop; exact remaining event count and run time are unknown.
next_versioned_prototype: Independent, default-off fast-path experiment may pass the already encoded event object alongside exact JSONL bytes to avoid duplicate parse, with equivalent schema/reference/operation checks and unchanged output bytes; benchmark against the same deterministic event stream, then assess budget reservation and fsync separately. No production Observer change until full synthetic and fault-injection review.
required_acceptance: Same logical sequence, per-event bytes and full-stream SHA for all generated test events; no sampling or field loss.
Same array occurrence binding, operation boundary checks, 4 GiB storage budget and completion semantics.
Failure injection preserves business exceptions and yields invalid evidence, never a false completion.
Streaming validation and strict B/C comparison unchanged.
No business planner, guard, ownership, RNG or pathology witness call during offline prototype tests.
A new real S07 run would require a fresh reviewed manifest and separate one-shot authorization.
